question: Which of the following ratios is the greatest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert each ratio to its approximate **decimal value** to compare quickly.

48 : 90 ≈ 0.533

46 : 51 ≈ 0.902 (closest to 1)

22 : 54 ≈ 0.407

42 : 68 ≈ 0.617

**∴ The correct answer is 46 : 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20173f1d647584574fad5ce2aa6bc5a506019e4162c767836bb37d7e1bb45fef.png] 

**Given Ratios:** 48/90, 46/51, 22/54, 42/68

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio 1 = 48 ÷ 90 = 0.533...

⇒ Ratio 2 = 46 ÷ 51 = 0.9019...

⇒ Ratio 3 = 22 ÷ 54 = 0.4074...

⇒ Ratio 4 = 42 ÷ 68 = 0.6176...

⇒ Comparing values: 0.9019 > 0.6176 > 0.5333 > 0.4074

**∴ The correct answer is 46 : 51.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Comparison Rule

To compare ratios a:b and c:d, compare the products (a×d) and (b×c). If ad > bc, then a/b > c/d.

Proper Fraction Property

In a proper fraction (numerator < denominator), as the difference between numerator and denominator decreases, the value of the fraction approaches 1.

Percentage Method

Converting ratios to percentages (Ratio × 100) is another effective way to identify the greatest or smallest ratio.</p
